narrative: OMX30 inherits positive European momentum this morning with DAX and CAC outperforming on stable macro backdrop. The index sits 4.6% above its 200-day moving average in bull regime, underpinned by a fresh MACD bullish crossover and robust 90-day ROC of +6.9%, positioning it near 52-week highs (-1.6% from peak). However, weak ADX reading (3.7) signals trend fragility and justifies cautious stance; RSI at neutral 51.81 offers no mean-reversion warning. Yield compression on the US 10Y (-0.44%) eases tech valuation pressure despite NASDAQ flat, while commodity strength (copper +0.82%, Brent +0.70%) creates offsetting drags on input-cost sensitive sectors. Key watch: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET could trigger volatility into close.
morningBrief: OMX30 set to open modestly higher on inherited European equity strength and MACD bullish structure, targeting 3123–3140 range. Industrials (Volvo B, Atlas Copco A) and Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) in focus: exporters benefit from USD/SEK weakness despite oil headwind, while banks see stable NIM outlook on flatter US curve. Boliden screams long on copper +0.82%—direct commodity revenue play. Watch Ericsson/Hexagon for tech sentiment given NASDAQ flatness. ADX weakness (3.7) caps upside conviction; treat +0.4% expected move as ceiling, not floor. Key technical: hold above 3085 (lower Bollinger band) to maintain rhythm; resistance at 3180 (50-MA). US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET—risk event into close. H&M B under pressure: EUR/SEK weakness (+0.45%) inflates sourcing costs despite consumer defensiveness. Maintain disciplined risk management; this is a consolidation day, not a breakout.
